text:
bryan: Heads-up, customer reported structured-output validation failures after last night's canary swap in prod-eu. They say enums are being returned with different values/order and their schema validator is rejecting payloads. Ticket #CS-12489.
janet (customer): our webhook started getting 422s around 03:18 UTC. validators that used to accept the response now fail with 'unexpected enum value'. example below.
janet (customer): Request snippet:
```json
{
  "model": "rl3b-8k-v3q",
  "input": "Generate a JSON with fields \"id,priority\" where priority is one of [P0,P1,P2]."
}
```
janet (customer): Response we got (previously was P1):
```json
{
  "id": "42",
  "priority": "P2"
}
```
bryan: Can you confirm which model you were on right before the swap and whether you pinned a model version?
janet (customer): We were on rl3b-8k-v2 pinned implicitly by route; yesterday at 03:10 the canary swapped to rl3b-8k-v3q. No explicit schema mapping on our side.
oliver: I can reproduce quickly with a local call to v3q vs v2. Looks like enum outputs are being remapped — same set of tokens but different canonical choice for ties/softmax ordering (P1 vs P2). Also seeing minor latency bump (~25-40ms) for the new variant. Might be tokenization/prompt-conditioning change in the model artifact.
meera: Running tokenization diff now. Preliminary: v3q's quantization introduced token merges for the P* tokens which changes generation probabilities in tight prompts. That combined with beam/temp settings leads to different top choice. Not a runtime bug per-se, it's a model-behavior change (schema drift).
meera: Repro steps I used: exact same prompt, seed, and deterministic sampler; v2 -> priority:P1, v3q -> priority:P2 in ~60% of runs.
anya: For the customer, temporary mitigations?
oliver: Short term: 1) rollback route to rl3b-8k-v2 (fastest), 2) add a small mapping transform at the console edge to remap unexpected enum values to canonical set, or 3) ask customer to relax validator to accept both values.
bryan: I'll offer rollback + mapping. Can we automate a mapping rule with small cost?
oliver: Yes I can add a per-route post-processing mapping rule (string->string) — low risk. I'll open infra change and schedule rollback.
deploy-bot: rollback job created: job/rl3b-eu-rollback-1987654321, ETA 3m.
janet (customer): Please do rollback, mapping is fine as temporary. Appreciate quick help.
meera: Long term: ML to retrain/refreeze tokenization/decoding for rl3b-v3 variants or publish a note in model catalog about enum-sensitive schema changes when switching quantized variants. Also add unit evals for a collection of structured-output prompts.
oliver: Filed internal task INFRA-7942 to add auto-eval for enums and structured outputs on canary rollouts.
bryan: I'll follow up with CS to confirm rollback success and mark ticket CS-12489 resolved once customer verifies. :thumbsup:
anya: pinging customer once rollback completes.
janet (customer): rollback completed on our side, validations passing again. thanks! :pray:
